name: City Council Special Meeting of November 12, 2024

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  OF NOVEMBER 12, 2024

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE PARKING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
WATER AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Martin Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Councilmember Puente
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Ruedas  7-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  This is the time set aside for interested members of the public to address the City Council
  on agendized Closed Session matters. Subject to the commenting procedures described
  above, the City Council will allow interested members of the public to address the City
  Council on agendized Closed Session matters prior to holding Closed Session. Each
  speaker will be given a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total
  to address the Council on any or all closed session items of business. The City Council
  shall be under no obligation to recognize a speaker who submits a speaker card after the
  City Council has gone into Closed Session.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 and 4.2.

  Matthew Waken – Spoke about the current stage of his project.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:11 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:33 p.m.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8 – Conference with
  Real Property Negotiator:

  Proper Location:
  8575-017-909, 8575-019-907, 8575-019-908, 8575-019-910, 8575-019-911,
  8575-019-912, 8575-019-913, 8575-021-932, 8575-021-934, 8575-021-936

  Name of Party City is Negotiating with:
  Area Y El Monte, LLC

  City’s Representative in Negotiations:
  Alma K. Martinez, City Manager

  Under Discussion:
  Discussion of price and terms.

  No Reportable Final Action Taken.
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 12, 2024

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; and El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager; and Rigoberto
  Gutierrez, Human Resources/Risk Management Director

  No Reportable Final Action Taken.

5.  INVOCATION:  City Council. Chaplain George Ussery. Present

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Sofia Perez from Parkview Elementary School

7.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items). Each speaker will be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous
  minutes total to address the Council on any or all matters covered by this section. As
  explained more specifically under the Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of
  the public wishing to offer comment on items of business agendized under the Public
  Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a separate allotment of three (3) continuous
  minutes per speaker per public hearing item. Except as otherwise provided under the
  Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.), the Council may not deliberate or take
  action upon any matter not listed on this posted agenda but may order that any such
  matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent meeting. The Council may also direct
  staff to investigate certain matters for consideration at a future meeting. Persons wishing
  to address the Council on matters covered under General Public Comment shall submit a
  speaker card in the manner prescribed in this agenda, above, by or before the General
  Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no
  obligation to entertain comments from speakers who submit cards to speak on matters
  covered by the section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Jesse Fierro – Spoke about a citation he received from Code Enforcement.

  Julio M. Ramirez – Spoke about the agenda and Congratulated the Mayor.

9.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda. One
  or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be discussed,
  considered, and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be removed from
  the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded motion of any
  member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council quorum.

9.3  Consideration and Approval of Purchase Orders with Two (2) Vendors for Police
  Department Duty Ammunition and Practice Ammunition on an As-Needed Basis.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Consider and approve the selection of Dooley Enterprises and San Diego
  Police Equipment to serve on the El Monte Police Department’s Bench List of
  suppliers for purchase of practice ammunition and duty ammunition;
  2. Consider and approve Purchase Orders with the two (2) selected ammunition
  suppliers on an as-needed basis for cumulative not-to-exceed amount of
  $100,000; and
  3. Authorize the City Manager, and/or the Chief of Police, to administratively
  manage the Purchase Agreements and/or approved Purchase Order funds for
  the approved vendors, as needed, through the City’s internal Change Order

  City of El Monte;

  expense account numbers and corresponding revenue account numbers and
  authorize the use of SHSP grant monies for this budget amendment; and

  the County of Los Angeles, and all amendments thereof.

  Downtown Mural Art Program; Extend the Downtown Mural Program for a Period
  of Two (2) Years; and Reallocate $100,000 from the Art in Public Places Fund for

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  1. Extend the Downtown Mural Program for a period of two (2) years and
  reallocate $100,000 from the Art in Public Places Fund for the Downtown Mural

  2. Approve an increase in expenditure in the amount of $87,283.15 for the
  “Memories of El Monte” mural for a new total not-to-exceed amount of
  $182,283.15;
  3. Approve a Professional Services Agreement with Ignacio Gomez Studio for the
  “Memories of El Monte” mural in the amount of $182,283.15 (Attachment 1);
  and
  4. Authorize the City Manager to enter into and execute the Professional Services
  Agreement.

10.3  Consideration and Approval of Purchase Orders with 25 Vehicle Maintenance,

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  PAC; Interstate Battery; Advance Auto Parts; AutoZone; Detroit Auto Parts;
  Kimball Midwest; Dr.’s Autoglass; A & A Auto Wrecking; Classic Custom Tint;
  Performance Ford; and Napa Auto Parts to serve on the El Monte Police
  Department’s (the “Police Department”) Bench List of suppliers for vehicle
  maintenance, parts and supplies services;
  2. Consider and approve the selection of seven (7) vendors: ABS of South El
  Monte; Bumper Express; Autosquare Collision Center; Dana Safety Supply
  Inc.; 10-8 Retrofit; JBC Electronics; and AV Auto Collision Center to serve on
  the Police Department’s Bench List of suppliers for auto body repairs;
  3. Consider and approve Purchase Orders with the 25 selected vehicle
  maintenance, auto body repair and parts vendors on an as-needed basis for
  cumulative not-to-exceed amount of $280,000; and
  4. Authorize the City Manager and/or the Chief of Police to administratively
  manage the Purchase Agreements and/or approved Purchase Order funds for
  the approved vendors, as needed, through the City’s internal Change Order
  process.

  Total Cost: $280,000  Account No:  100-71-711-6335
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? Yes

  2. Authorize an appropriation in the amount of $200,000 for Fiscal Year 2024/25

  3. Authorize the SGVCOG to reimburse $200,000 to the General Fund for the

  Department;
  4. Consider and approve CDCE Incorporated, which utilized and followed, the
  State of California Participating Addendum Number 7-23-70-55-10 under the

  5. Authorize the City Manager, or the Chief of Police, to sign all necessary

11.  ADJOURNMENT:  Adjourn in Memory of Ernesto Villegas.

  City Manager Martinez – Gave an update on the Tabacco Grant that was just awarded to
  the City.

  Councilmember Maritnez Muela – Requested a discussion regarding opening City
  facilities for community use. Requested at the next meeting a list of what events have
  been cut due to budget Requested a review of the Organization Chart to fill open positions.

  Mayor Ancona – Received a call from the ERA president to see if the City would be willing
  to contribute $10,000 towards their cause to help the 500 families.

  Councilmember Herrera – Mentioned that there were no Council Communication
  agendized for the meeting. Wanted to make sure that the Council is not giving direction
  on items that weren’t agendized.

  Assistant City Attorney Pilchen – Indicated that are an informal thing and that as long as
  the items are not deliberated on an action but merely giving direction items don’t have to
  be agendized. Just don’t deliberate on an item make a request to bring back at later date.

  Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Ruedas: Requested a presentation regarding the Tabacco Grant.

  City Manager Martinez informed the City Council that this item will be brought to the City
  Council at the next meeting for approval.
